FRST 100.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 100.description: An overview of forests and forestry. Survey of the disciplines, areas of study, and values that frame sustainable management of forests in BC and the world. Assignments focus on critical thinking and written communication skills. [3-0-0]

FRST 101.course_name: Principles of Microeconomics for Forestry and Land and Food Systems
FRST 101.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 101.description: Principles of microeconomics and their applications in forestry and land and food systems. The basic concept of the economy to focus on private and social decision making related to the use of land, especially in agriculture, forestry, and conservation. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST 101, ECON 101, or LFS 101. [3-0-1] Equivalency: LFS101, ECON101

FRST 107.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 107.description: An introduction to Forestry Co-op including: completion of preemployment workshops, career skills toolkits, networking opportunities, interview training, individual coaching sessions, and job search skills. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship Co-operative Education Program. Pass/fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 110.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 110.description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both First Nations and Western perspectives. [2-0-1;2-0-1] Equivalency: LFS_V 110, NRES_V 110. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 150.course_name: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Forestry
FRST 150.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 150.description: Communicating concepts of forestry and links to human and environmental activities through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 150, FRST_V 150, or LFS_V 150. [3-0-0] Equivalency: LFS_V 150, NRES_V 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 200.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 200.description: The structure, diversity and development of trees and other plants, with emphasis on the angiosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 200 or FRST 200. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: BIOL 121. Equivalency: NRES 200

FRST 201.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 201.description: The structure and function of forest ecosystems, including: energetics; productivity; nutrient, carbon and water cycling; soils; the physical environment; population and community ecology; disturbance ecology; ecological succession; biological diversity and ecological resilience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 201 or FRST 201. [3-2-0] Equivalency: NRES 201

FRST 202.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 202.description: The Ecosystem concept; energy biomass and nutrient cycling; the physical environment; population and community ecology; succession, Biogeoclimatic classification and some coastal ecosystems. Available only through Distance Education. [3-2]

FRST 203.course_name: Silvics of Forest Trees of Western Canada
FRST 203.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 203.description: Ecological and silvical characteristics of forest trees; assessment of ecological site quality and biogeoclimatic classification; application of silvics in silviculture. A plant herbarium of at least 50 species is required. Only available through Distance Education. [3-2] Prerequisite: FRST202

FRST 210.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 210.description: The functional biology of trees and other forest plants in their environment, with an emphasis on gymnosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 210 or FRST 210. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 200, NRES 200. Equivalency: NRES 210.

FRST 211.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 211.description: Forest classification and the application of silvics in forest management, including world forest classification systems, the Biogeoclimactic Ecosystem Classification system, and ecosystem diagnosis in the field. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 211 or FRST 211. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201. Equivalency: NRES 211

FRST 231.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 231.description: Basic theories of probability and statistics. Sampling distribution, methods of estimation and hypothesis testing; goodness of fit and tests for independence; analysis of variance, regression and correlation. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 231 or FRST 231. [3-2-0] Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 180, MATH 184, MATH 190. Equivalency: NRES 231

FRST 232.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 232.description: Techniques involved in solving forestry problems with microcomputers using word processing, spreadsheet, procedural language, and database management tools. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 232 or FRST 232. [3-2] Equivalency: NRES 232

FRST 239.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 239.description: An introduction to measurement of individual trees and stands; use of aerial photographs, maps, and various measurement instruments. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 231, NRES 231 and one of FRST 232, NRES 232.

FRST 248.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 248.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Orientation workshops required. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 302.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 302.description: Population genetics and conservation of genetic resources; principles of genetics and their application to forestry. [2-2]

FRST 303.course_name: Into the Woods: An Introduction to Forest Science
FRST 303.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 303.description: Introduction to growth of trees and forests with emphasis on evolutionary, ecological and environmental aspects. Not available for credit to undergraduate students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. [3-0-0]

FRST 304.course_name: Forest Stewardship in a Changing Climate
FRST 304.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 304.description: Forests can provide natural solutions to climate change and social well-being through innovative management and restoration including protection of mother trees and soils, carbon and conservation financing, and emergence of value-added industries. For students without strong science backgrounds. Not available for credit to Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship students. [3-0-0]

FRST 305.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 305.description: Silviculture concepts and principles; stand dynamics; artificial and natural regeneration; cultural techniques for forest stand establishment and stand tending; silvicultural systems; decision making and development of prescriptions; connections to forest planning. [3-4*] Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201 and one of FRST 350, FRST 351, UFOR 400.

FRST 307.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 307.description: Concepts of disturbance ecology with special reference to insects and diseases in the forests of British Columbia; forest health problems in the biogeoclImatic zones of BC; present management strategies and future potentials in a scenario of climate change. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211.

FRST 308.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 308.description: An introduction to insects that cause damage to forests and forest products; how insects live; life cycles and attack symptoms of representatives of major groups of insects; principles for control and management. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 309.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 309.description: Biology and management of forest tree diseases. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 310.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 310.description: The diversity and interactions of soil organisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi, animals, plants) in natural and managed ecosystems; roles in primary production, nutrient cycling, decomposition and reclamation; responses to environmental change. [2-3-0] Prerequisite: BIOL 121. Equivalency: APBI342

FRST 311.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 311.description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. CHEM 203, CHEM 213, or CHEM 233 and CHEM 235 is recommended. [3-3-0] Equivalency: BIOL351, APBI351

FRST 318.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 318.description: Practical problem solving of economic issues related to forestry and conservation, touching on investment analysis, capital budgeting, non-timber economics, ecosystem services, and forest certification. Completion of FRST 232 or NRES 232 or intermediate knowledge of MS Excel essential. [2-3-0] Prerequisite: One of ECON 101, FRST 101.

FRST 319.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 319.description: Introduction to the economics of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services produced by, and dependent on, the forest resource. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 320.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 320.description: Ecological effects of fire and climatic (wind, temperature, and snow) disturbances; fire danger rating, principles of fire management and prescribed fire use; windthrow risk modelling and management. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211.

FRST 339.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 339.description: Obtaining and forecasting information for stands and forests. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: FRST 239.

FRST 346.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 346.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 347.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 347.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 348.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 348.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 350.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 350.description: Field study concentrating on outdoor skills, forest measurements, site diagnosis, and an integrated overview of the ecological, social and economic basis for forest management. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST_V 350 or 351. Prerequisite: FRST_V 211 or NRES_V 211; FRST_V 201 or NRES_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 351.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 351.description: Field study at an interior BC location concentrating on land use, management and silviculture. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Students with FRST_V 351 and FRST_V 350 can only count 3 credits toward their program requirements. Prerequisite: FRST_V 210 or NRES_V 210. Corequisite: FRST_V 211 or NRES_V 211.

FRST 370.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 370.description: Community forests and community forestry throughout the world, with special attention to participation by aboriginal peoples; emphasis is on forms of governance, public participation, and adaptive learning. [3-0-0]

FRST 385.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 385.description: Measurement and analysis of hydrological processes in response to forest management activities. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.

FRST 386.course_name: Aquatic Ecosystems and Fish in Forested Watersheds
FRST 386.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 386.description: Effects of forest management activities on fish and aquatic ecosystems. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing in Forestry, Science, Applied Science or Applied Biology.

FRST 395.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 395.description: Ecology, management, and conservation of terrestrial vertebrate wildlife, focusing primarily on socio-economically important, forest-dwelling species of mammals, birds, amphibians and reptiles. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, BIOL 230, BIOL 306.

FRST 399.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 399.description: Lectures and seminars in research philosophies and the scientific method, with special emphasis on field research. [2-1] Prerequisite: One of FRST 150, LFS 150, NRES 150, WRDS 150, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, WOOD 225, NRES 225.

FRST 402.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 402.description: Multi-disciplinary course in which students, individually and in groups, examine, integrate and apply subject-specific knowledge through the lens of language and the framework of the language sciences, with a focus on themes of real-world importance. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor. Equivalency: APSC402, ASTU402, LFS 402, LLED402, PHAR402

FRST 403.course_name: The Sustainability of Production in Managed Forest Ecosystems
FRST 403.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 403.description: Study of the functional and dynamic characteristics of forest ecosystems and their response to forest management using ecosystem-level microcomputer simulation models. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201.

FRST 404.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 404.description: Fundamental silvicultural problems; the application of research findings to the practice of silviculture. [4-0] Prerequisite: FRST 305.

FRST 406.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 406.description: Hereditary, physiological, anatomical, environmental, and microbiological factors influencing forest tree diseases. Given in alternate years. [2-2]

FRST 408.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 408.description: Role of climate and climate change in the population dynamics, outbreak potentials and resultant impacts to forest ecosystems associated with herbivorous forest insects. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 307, APBI 327, BIOL 327.

FRST 410.course_name: Introduction to Landscape Ecology and Management
FRST 410.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 410.description: Current concepts, methods, and applications of landscape ecology with emphasis on spatial patterning, spatial heterogeneity, and dynamics; problem-solving approaches to natural resource issues through the application of landscape ecological principles and tools. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 411.course_name: Complex Adaptive Systems, Global Change Science, and Ecology Sustainability
FRST 411.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 411.description: Concepts of complex adaptive systems (CAS); exploration of how CAS can be used to manage natural and social environments for multiple goals under changing climatic and socio-economic conditions. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing

FRST 413.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 413.description: The structure, biosynthesis, distribution and biological function of secondary plant metabolites. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 201 and one of BIOL 209, BIOL 210; or (b) one of FRST 200, NRES 200 and one of FRST 210, NRES 210. Equivalency: BIOL462

FRST 415.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 415.description: The development, implementation, and analysis of forest policy. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.

FRST 421.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 421.description: Introduction to the quantitative tools necessary in forest management. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 422.course_name: Mathematical Modelling in Forest Resource Analysis
FRST 422.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 422.description: Modelling techniques used in strategic and tactical forest resources analyses. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in the BSF degree.

FRST 423.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 423.description: Forest management designs to identify and integrate economic, social, and environmental objectives across a forested landscape both strategically and tactically. [4-2-2] Prerequisite: FRST 422.

FRST 425.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 425.description: Analyze and interpret existing management plans, prescribe solutions for achieving specific forest management goals at multiple scales, use basic tools to evaluate the financial implications of such solutions, and create a forest management plan for a virtual forest. Offered entirely online. Students in any of the Forestry programs requiring FRST 423 (6 cr) in order to graduate will not be granted the 3 cr of FRST 425 toward degree completion.

FRST 430.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 430.description: Analysis of variance, multiple regression and analysis of covariance. Design and analysis of experiments. [3-2] Prerequisite: One of FRST 231, NRES 231, BIOL 300, STAT 200. And FRST 399 or equivalent. Restricted to students with 4th year standing or by permission of instructor.

FRST 432.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 432.description: The genomic basis of adaptation to environments. Topics progress through community structure, life history patterns, stress responses, and variation and adaptation. [3-0-0]

FRST 436.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 436.description: Techniques of growth and yield projection and discussion of modelling approaches. Exploration of stand dynamics, quantitative implications of management treatments and environmental limitations to tree and stand growth. [2-2-0] Prerequisite: FRST339

FRST 439.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 439.description: The socio-economic, biological and technological aspects of forestry within the international frame, in both the developed and developing world. Regional studies and the role of national and international agencies. [2-2-0]

FRST 443.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 443.description: Basic biological concepts related to interpretation of remote sensing data for land management, including the use of films and filters, and interpretation of air photographs, and other imagery. [2-2-0]

FRST 444.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 444.description: Ecological, economic and social benefits of incorporating trees into agricultural landscapes. Lectures and groupwork designing agroforestry systems in temperate and tropical contexts. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201, APBI 260. Equivalency: APBI444

FRST 446.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 446.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 447.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 447.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 448.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 448.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 449.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 449.description: In special cases and with the approval of the instructor concerned, a student may carry on directed studies of specific problems in forestry.

FRST 452.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 452.description: Site diagnosis and preparation of management options in coastal forests. Extrasessional course; fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Prerequisite: FRST_V 350 or 351; FRST_V 305; Third- or fourth-year standing in the B.S.F. program, or Forest Management major or Forest Operations major in B.Sc. in Natural Resources program.

FRST 456.course_name: The Role of Natural and Planted Forests in the Global Bioeconomy
FRST 456.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 456.description: (Go Global Seminar Series) An intensive one-month field school in Chile focused on fast-growing industrial forest plantations, innovative wood products, land use strategies for natural and planted forests, and their impact on society. Prerequisite: Third-year standing

FRST 470.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 470.description: Social aspects of forestry and forest communities. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.

FRST 475.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 475.description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes. Prerequisite: One of BEST_V 203, BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, APBI_V 260, GEOS_V 207. And third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 485.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 485.description: Effects of land management on quality, quantity and timing of water flow. [3-2-0] Prerequisite: FRST385

FRST 490.course_name: Visual Resource Management and Planning for Aesthetics
FRST 490.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 490.description: Methodologies for visual analysis, perceptions, planning & management of urban, natural and working landscapes, and implications for sustainable land-use management & community engagement. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST 490 or FRST 551. [2-2] Prerequisite: Third-year standing. Equivalency: LARC542

FRST 491.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 491.description: GIS-based spatial planning and 3D landscape visualization for forest management. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.

FRST 492.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 492.description: How individuals perceive their environment. Emphasis will be given visual perception in the context of natural resource issues and the effects of those perceptions on individuals including issues of human wellbeing. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing

FRST 495.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 495.description: Principles, problems, and practices of managing natural habitats for biological diversity; current issues in biological diversity important to researchers, policymakers, and the general public. [2-2-0]. Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 201, NRES_V 201 and FRST_V 395. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 497.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 497.description: Preparing professional reports and presentations; professionalism and professional ethics. [2-0-2] Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing.

FRST 498.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 498.description: An independent study or research project of a subject of special interest to the student under the direction of a staff member. Available only to students in the BSFS Honours specialization.

FRST 499.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 499.description: An independent study or research project on an approved topic, developed under the guidance of a Faculty member. Available only to students in their graduating year.

FRST 500.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 500.description: An evidence-based examination of teaching and learning in forestry, focusing on instructional design, classroom practices and field instruction. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 502.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 502.description: Evolution and current structure, functions and diversity of moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the humid tropics. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 503.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 503.description: Techniques of purification, cloning, sequencing, restriction-hybridization analysis of plant nucleic acids, in-vitro labeling of plant nucleic acids and proteins, and electrophoresis and immunodetection of plant proteins. Offered by the Biotechnology Teaching Laboratory in cooperation with the Department of Forest and Conservation Sciences. Admission to the course is limited and requires recommendation from the department head. Equivalency: PLNT_V 540, BOTA_V 544. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 504.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 504.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 505.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 505.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 506.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 506.description: Hereditary, physiological, anatomical, environmental, and microbiological factors influencing forest tree diseases. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 507.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 507.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 508.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 508.description: Role of climate and climate change in the population dynamics, outbreak potentials and resultant impacts to forest ecosystems associated with herbivorous forest insects. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 509.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 509.description: Linear model theory and application for observational data and randomized experiments. Multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of covariance. Design and analysis of experiments. Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 231, NRES_V 231, BIOL_V 300, or STAT_V 200. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 510.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 510.description: Equivalency: BIOL_V 510. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 512.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 512.description: Review of current literature on specific topics in forest soil ecology, including bacterial endophytes, microbial diversity, nutrient cycling, and mycorrhizae. Students with either APBI_V 412 or CONS_V 412 will not be allowed to take FRST_V 512. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 513.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 513.description: Advanced research topics and their application to forest genetics. Emphasis on molecular genetics and experimental protocols. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 335 or permission of the instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 515.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 515.description: Psychological, social, and systemic dimensions of climate change communication; approaches for engaging diverse groups for low-carbon futures; overcoming climate inaction. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 516.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 516.description: Growth and development of woody plants; physiological responses to abiotic and biotic environmental factors; consequences of silvicultural practices on physiological processes. [3-2] Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 311, BIOL_V 351, APBI_V 351. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 517.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 517.description: Applying economics to forest and forestland management, including analysis of how government policies and market designs affect forest management outcomes. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 518.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 518.description: Political ecology of resource extraction. History of the extractive corporate form. Theories of land ownership, access, and sovereignty in relation to market forces. Tensions between society, state, and the market. Global approaches to governing extraction. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 519.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 519.description: Emphasis on tropical and sub-tropical countries, where the majority of forest-dependent people live. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 520.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 520.description: Applications of advanced theory and quantitative analysis to problems in forest resource and land economics; multiple land use; institutions for sustainable land use; optimal management and policy. [3-0] Equivalency: AGEC_V 520. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 521.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 521.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 522.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 522.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 523.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 523.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 524.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 524.description: Perceptual processes mediating behaviour in humans, with special attention given to the emotional processing of visual stimuli. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 525.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 525.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 526.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 526.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 527.course_name: People and Forests: An International Perspective
FRST 527.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 527.description: Biodiversity loss, deforestation, desertification, salinization, air pollution and climate change facing world forests. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST_V 439 or FRST_V 527. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 528.course_name: Social Science Research Methods for Forestry and Conservation
FRST 528.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 528.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 529.faculty: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
FRST 529.description: Emphasis on forested ecosystems. Prerequisite: ECON_V 301. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

FRST 530.course_name: Advanced Modelling Methods for Natural Resources Applications
